## 92953d9974a2

**Finding type: reproduced canonical-control coverage defect and shortcut.**
Generator SHA-256
`bef5869b3d9873de266b4f5ead26cd2e3d71f32b6cd1b095ff32d5b5021432bf`;
executed canonical rule hash `0949ff4df9d3`.

The canonical task uses the bottom-left cell as a rotation code: `1` identity,
`2` rotate 90°, `3` rotate 180°, and the remaining canonical value `4` selects
the fourth transform. The normal generator does not construct that code cell.
It starts from background 0 and draws motif colors only from
`[2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9]`; therefore code `1` is unreachable by construction, while
code `0` is common whenever no random motif lands at the bottom-left.

A deterministic census of seeds `0..199`, sample index `0`, in each of easy,
medium, and hard materialized all 600 draws with no generation failure. Code 1
appeared **0/600** times. Code 0 appeared 196/200 easy, 186/200 medium, and
194/200 hard—**576/600 overall**. The three labeled canonical inputs use codes
`2`, `4`, and `3`, and the written rule explicitly defines the four-code family.

The retained seed-0 easy witness has bottom-left code 0 and passes `self_check`.
Canonical Racket therefore takes its catch-all transpose branch. Changing only
the bottom-left cell to code 1 yields a different canonical Racket output,
showing that the missing setting changes the transformation. This is both an
out-of-domain selector value in most generated inputs and a complete omission of
the identity branch from generated training data.

Evidence: `checks/audit/92953d9974a2/census.json`,
`checks/audit/92953d9974a2/counterexample.json`,
`checks/audit/92953d9974a2/racket.json`, and
`checks/audit/92953d9974a2/code1_racket.json`. The code-0 witness is generated
and accepted by the target validator; the code-1 counterfactual belongs to the
documented rule family but is unreachable from the normal sampler. No
audit-target source was changed.
